exports.trimFlacAudio: (frames: AsyncIterable<AudioFrameData>, range: FlacAudioTrimRange, options: FlacAudioTrimOptions) => AsyncIterable<AudioFrameData>
exports.FlacAudioTrimRange: {startSample: bigint, endSampleExclusive: bigint | null, outputPtsSamples: bigint}

semantics.range: Zero-based decoded sample ordinals, end exclusive, null means EOF. Negative start or end before start is rejected. Input PTS is not the selection clock.
semantics.pts: Always contiguous from outputPtsSamples, timeBase {num: 1n, den: BigInt(sampleRate)}.
semantics.formatChanges: Rejected; channels, layout, sample rate, and sample format must remain stable.
semantics.bounds: Each decoded frame must be <= maxFrameBytes, selected output allocation must also be <= resources.budget.maxBufferBytes. No full-stream retention. No upstream pull beyond the frame containing the exclusive end.

lifetime.input: Producer-owned; adapter never mutates input. Source next/return must manage any decoder leases because AudioFrameData has no release method.
lifetime.output: Copied planes are borrowed until next(), return(), throw(), or abort. Retaining consumers must make their own Core-accounted copy.
lifetime.memory: One actual PCM allocation, reserveExternalMemory(bytes) before new Uint8Array(bytes), retained across yield and released before the next pull, on failure, return, throw, or either signal abort. Array/view/runtime bookkeeping is not charged by Core's media-byte accounting.
lifetime.cancellation: Both options.signal and resources.signal are observed. Pending next is interrupted; upstream return is requested once; late next/return rejections are observed. Idle explicit return awaits cooperative source cleanup and propagates cleanup failures; either signal can interrupt that wait. Pending-read return and abort detach without waiting for uncooperative providers, whose cleanup may complete later.

integration: Exported by packages/avformat/src/index.ts and called by packages/avformat/src/flac-transform.ts for timed transforms. The coordinator-owned backend runs bounded sequential count and output passes and publishes through the existing atomic output group. Wrap decoder frame leases in an AsyncIterable<AudioFrameData> whose next/return release the prior lease. Use countTrimmedFlacSamples only with a known actual decoded length (FLAC totalSamples=0 may mean unknown). The helper performs no I/O.
